OCTOBER 2026 Haryana 24 News Network v. Union of India A Superintendent of Police sent Meta a s. 79(3)(b) notice. The news company's Facebook page was blocked on 21 August 2026. It got no notice and no copy. (Justice Tribhuvan Dahiya) 1 Without jurisdiction. An SP is below the DIG rank Rule 3(1)(d) requires. The notice was set aside. 2 Give the user a copy. When the notice goes to the platform, a copy must go to the user too. The court read this into the Rules. 3 No futile remedies. The user needn't first use Meta's grievance process; without the grounds, there's nothing to answer. ✓ Page restored within 24 hours of the order reaching the SP. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 04 / 08

KERALA HIGH COURT · 26 OCTOBER 2026 Hyder Ali K. v. Union of India (NoCap) THE FACTS An in-app message, and nothing else On 28 September, Facebook told Malayalam news outlet NoCap that its content was restricted in India under a s. 79(3)(b) government notice. No order was published or shared, and there was no hearing. WHAT NOCAP SEEKS See the order, then challenge it Production of the order, a stay, restoration of the page, and a declaration that s. 79(3)(b) orders must be communicated to the affected user. WHAT THE COURT DID Asked the governments to explain Justice Ziyad Rahman A.A. asked the Centre and the State whether any order was sent to Meta, issued notice to Meta, and listed the case for 5 November. You can't challenge an order you can't see 1 Write user notice into Rule 3(1)(d). The P&H ruling binds only one High Court's territory. A rule would apply everywhere. 2 Share the reasons. The notice is already "reasoned"; the user should get those reasons, with narrow exceptions recorded in writing. 3 A hearing after the block. Where urgency rules out prior notice, a hearing within a fixed time afterwards. 4 Publish numbers. Release figures from the monthly reviews: notices sent, by whom, and how many were withdrawn. 5 Block the item, not the page. Rule 3(1)(d) targets specific URLs; restricting a whole news page should be the exception. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 06 / 08

PRACTICAL CHECKLIST If your page or account is blocked 1 Save the platform's message Screenshot the notice; it often names the provision (69A or 79(3)(b)). 2 Ask for the order Write to the platform's grievance officer; file an RTI with the department or police unit concerned. 3 Test it against Rule 3(1)(d) Rank and authorisation of the officer, written reasons, the law invoked, specific URLs. 4 Record your losses Followers, monetisation, subscriber revenue: evidence for urgency and interim relief. 5 Move the High Court early A writ under Article 226, relying on natural justice and the P&H ruling. Adv. Ashwani Kumar 07 / 08

TA K E AWAY A right you can't use is no right at all. Unlawful content can and should come down. But a citizen whose page is blocked must at least know who ordered it and why. Punjab & Haryana has said so. Kerala's answer comes on 5 November. Adv.
